3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: In the middle of the night, I was woken up by a knock on my bedroom door.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: Bruno was lying at the foot of my bed. He sat upright.

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: Bruno sat upright in his dog bed.

12.speaker: Narrator
12.text: I heard Pabel's voice in the hallway.

17.speaker: Pabel Adria
17.text: "Sorry to wake you, Your Majesty, but there's an apparently urgent call for you downstairs."

18.speaker: Pabel Adria
18.text: "Sorry, Romus, but there's an apparently urgent call for you downstairs."

19.speaker: Narrator
19.text: I heard Pabel's voice in the hallway.

20.speaker: Narrator
20.text: We walked through the palace corridors until we reached my study.

21.speaker: Narrator
21.text: An attendant stood ready with the blue phone. He informed me that Chancellor Emmerich Hegel was on the line.

22.speaker: Player_Romus
22.text: "All right. Come in and help me get dressed."

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: Pabel opened the door. Bruno jumped up on him, tail wagging.

29.speaker: Narrator
29.text: I quickly dressed and joined Pabel in the hallway. Bruno let out a whine of disappointment as I shut him back in the bedroom.

33.speaker: Narrator
33.text: I quickly dressed and joined Pabel in the hallway.

34.speaker: Player_Romus
34.text: "So, it's been a while since Qalus..."

35.speaker: Narrator
35.text: Pabel opened the door and briskly made his way over to the armoire.

36.speaker: Player_Romus
36.text: "I'd wag my tail if I had one."

37.speaker: Player_Romus
37.text: "Who wouldn't be happy to see you, Pabel?"

44.speaker: Narrator
44.text: Pabel turned around and gave me a strained look.

47.speaker: Narrator
47.text: Bruno sat down. Pabel gave him a pat on the head and briskly moved over to the armoire.

48.speaker: Narrator
48.text: Pabel let out a short laugh, then briskly moved over to the armoire.

49.speaker: Narrator
49.text: Pabel didn't smile. He briskly moved over to the armoire.

53.speaker: Pabel Adria
53.text: "It's only a phone call. A simple robe and slippers should do it."

54.speaker: Narrator
54.text: He pulled a deep blue silk robe out of the armoire. I stood in front of him as he draped it over my shoulders.

55.speaker: Narrator
55.text: He tied the sash, allowing his fingers to brush lightly against my waist.

60.speaker: Narrator
60.text: Once I was dressed, we walked through the palace corridors until we reached my study.

61.speaker: Player_Romus
61.text: "I can't stop thinking about our night together."

62.speaker: Player_Romus
62.text: "When can we see each other again? And by 'see', I mean..."

63.speaker: Player_Romus
63.text: "Why are you being so distant to me?"

64.speaker: Narrator
64.text: He took a step closer to me and spoke in a low voice.

65.speaker: Pabel Adria
65.text: "Neither can I. But we can't carry on like that here."

66.speaker: Pabel Adria
66.text: "As a servant, I'm used to creeping around in the shadows. But the King is always in the spotlight."

67.speaker: Pabel Adria
67.text: "I haven't forgotten about Qalus. But we can't carry on like that here."

68.speaker: Narrator
68.text: He took a step closer to me and spoke in a low voice.

69.speaker: Player_Romus
69.text: "I am the ruler of this country. I shouldn't have to hide my proclivities."

70.speaker: Player_Romus
70.text: "We'll come up with a cover story. You sleep in my room to help me with my night terrors."

71.speaker: Player_Romus
71.text: "Wait. How much 'creeping around' have you done?"

72.speaker: Player_Romus
72.text: "I've done some creeping of my own, you know. But it was easier as a prince."

77.speaker: Pabel Adria
77.text: "I'll be under extra scrutiny now because of your investigation. We need to be careful."

80.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
80.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.PoisonInvestigator_Lucita"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.PoisonInvestigator_Titus"] == true)  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.InvestigatePoisoning_NoPabel"] == false) == false

81.speaker: Pabel Adria
81.text: "Enough to know that passion can compromise caution to a dangerous degree."

82.speaker: Pabel Adria
82.text: "It's not just a proclivity,{RiziaDLCText.PabelToPlayer}, it's a crime. Being found out could land us both in prison or worse."

83.speaker: Pabel Adria
83.text: "Yes, you're under much more scrutiny now. There are eyes everywhere here."

84.speaker: Pabel Adria
84.text: "I don't want to subject you to that risk, {RiziaDLCText.PabelToPlayer}."

85.speaker: Pabel Adria
85.text: "I don't think anyone suspects anything yet. But we need to be careful."
85.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.PoisonInvestigator_Lucita"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.PoisonInvestigator_Titus"] == true)  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.InvestigatePoisoning_NoPabel"] == false) == false

86.speaker: Player_Romus
86.text: "There must be some way we can meet in total secrecy."

87.speaker: Player_Romus
87.text: "Careful there. I wouldn't want impure thoughts distracting me from my meeting."

88.speaker: Narrator
88.text: The shadow of a smile passed across his face.

90.speaker: Narrator
90.text: He tightened the sash and smoothed out the robe's folds, letting his hands linger on me for just a moment longer than necessary.

92.speaker: Player_Romus
92.text: "So, it's been a while since Qalus..."

96.speaker: Narrator
96.text: Pabel glanced behind us, then spoke in a low voice.

99.speaker: Player_Romus
99.text: "Any idea what this call is about?"

101.speaker: Pabel Adria
101.text: "It's on the blue phone, so it's a world leader. Your aide will have more information."

104.speaker: Player_Romus
104.text: "Any palace intrigue I need to know about?"

112.speaker: Pabel Adria
112.text: "Well, the entire staff knows about you and Duchess Azaro. But I assume you weren't trying to keep that a secret."

113.speaker: Pabel Adria
113.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Pabel"] <= 0) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Lucita_Together"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Lucita_CompromisingPhoto"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Pabel_Together"] == true)

120.speaker: Pabel Adria
120.text: "You've got an important phone call. I shouldn't bore you with irrelevant details."

121.speaker: Pabel Adria
121.text: "I would prefer my personal life to remain private, Your Majesty."

124.speaker: Player_Romus
124.text: "Any palace intrigue I need to know about?"

129.speaker: Pabel Adria
129.text: "Well, the entire staff knows about you and Duchess Azaro. But I assume you weren't trying to keep that a secret."

130.speaker: Pabel Adria
130.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Pabel"] <= 0) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Lucita_Together"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Pabel_Together"] == true)

131.speaker: Pabel Adria
131.text: "I would prefer my personal life to remain private, Your Majesty. My apologies."

141.speaker: Pabel Adria
141.text: "You've got an important phone call. I shouldn't bore you with irrelevant details."

142.speaker: Pabel Adria
142.text: "Only the usual nonsense. Everyone's still speculating about Her Highness' marriage prospects."
142.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Pabel"] <= 0) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Lucita_Together"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Lucita_CompromisingPhoto"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Pabel_Together"] == true) == false)

144.speaker: Player_Romus
144.text: "You're right, of course. I shouldn't sabotage my reign over a misguided dalliance."

146.speaker: Pabel Adria
146.text: "Our time will come someday. But not yet."

147.speaker: Pabel Adria
147.text: "We'll figure it out. But not today."

149.speaker: Pabel Adria
149.text: "Only the usual nonsense. Everyone's still speculating about Her Highness' marriage prospects."
149.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Pabel"] <= 0) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Lucita_Together"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Pabel_Together"] == true) == false)

152.speaker: Player_Romus
152.text: "Let's go. I shouldn't keep this mysterious caller waiting."

154.speaker: Player_Romus
154.text: "You'd better have a good reason for calling me this late, Chancellor."

155.speaker: Player_Romus
155.text: "I didn't expect to hear from you this soon."

156.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
156.text: "Is it late? I never did have a handle on the time difference."

157.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
157.text: "No? After the way things ended in Morella?"

160.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
160.text: "I'm truly sorry to disturb you at this hour. But we have unfinished business."

161.speaker: Player_Romus
161.text: "I'll say. I was wondering why you never responded to my speech at the AN."

166.speaker: Player_Romus
166.text: "Your apology is not accepted. We should be speaking in daylight hours, accompanied by our staff."

170.speaker: Player_Romus
170.text: "It's too late to change my mind about the nationalization vote. What's done is done."

171.speaker: Player_Romus
171.text: "You must be talking about the MITZ nationalization plan."

172.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
172.text: "I appreciated your words then, Mr. Toras, but I had to find out whether they would translate into actions."

178.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
178.text: "Of course. Needless to say, I was pleased you voted the way you did."

179.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
179.text: "The nationalization vote was a success. But the future of the Trade Zone is far from decided."

180.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
180.text: "Yes, the vote has concluded. But the future of the MITZ is by no means set in stone."

181.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
181.text: "I now see a unique chance for our two very different countries to cooperate."

182.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
182.text: "I wanted to talk man to man, for reasons that shall soon become evident."

186.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
186.text: "The nationalization vote was unsuccessful. But the future of the Trade Zone is far from decided."

187.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
187.text: "However, that does not mean an end to our chance for cooperation."

188.speaker: Player_Romus
188.text: "I'm happy to hear that. By voting for nationalization, I wanted to signal that Rizia and Valgsland are on the same side."

189.speaker: Player_Romus
189.text: "Why? I believe my vote against nationalization made my intentions clear enough."

193.speaker: Player_Romus
193.text: "I'm happy to hear that. I regretfully had to vote against nationalization to protect Rizia's interests, but I still think we're on the same side."

194.speaker: Player_Romus
194.text: "Yes, our differing opinions on the MITZ shouldn't keep us from making other agreements."

198.speaker: Player_Romus
198.text: "I have changed my mind. I don't wish to cooperate with Malenyevists."

199.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
199.text: "In fact, with your vote comes a unique chance for cooperation."

200.speaker: Player_Romus
200.text: "The Democratic Republic of Valgsland would deign to cooperate with a monarchy?"

204.speaker: Player_Romus
204.text: "I had my reasons for choosing nationalization. Cooperating with Valgsland wasn't one of them."

205.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
205.text: "Despite your refusal to grant self-determination to Morella and its mines, I still see a chance for cooperation between us."

206.speaker: Player_Romus
206.text: "I don't wish to cooperate with Malenyevists."

210.speaker: Player_Romus
210.text: "I'm happy to hear that. I regretfully had to vote against nationalization, but I still think we're on the same side."

211.speaker: Player_Romus
211.text: "You're right. Our differing opinions on the MITZ shouldn't keep us from making other agreements."

212.speaker: Player_Romus
212.text: "The Democratic Republic of Valgsland would deign to cooperate with a monarchy?"

213.speaker: Player_Romus
213.text: "Despite both of us being in favor of nationalization, I'm skeptical we can reconcile our worldviews."

214.speaker: Player_Romus
214.text: "I voted for nationalization precisely so that you and I could have this conversation, Chancellor."

215.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
215.text: "There is only one thing we need to agree on."

216.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
216.text: "Any country ruled by a king is not on Valgsland's side, Mr. Toras. But there is one point we can agree on."

217.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
217.text: "Our politics need not factor into this. There is only one point we have to agree on."

218.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
218.text: "The Republic of Lespia does not belong in the Meftiem International Trade Zone."

219.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
219.text: "Not normally. But in this instance, there is one point we can agree on."

220.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
220.text: "Do not think that this somehow makes us allies, Mr. Toras. But there is one point we can both agree on."

221.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
221.text: "We do not have to like each other, Mr. Toras. There is only one point we have to agree on."

222.speaker: Player_Romus
222.text: "Another east-west battle? You should know that as a member of GRACE, Rizia is obliged to stay uninvolved."

223.speaker: Player_Romus
223.text: "Indeed. The future of the MITZ belongs to the workers and those who support them."

227.speaker: Player_Romus
227.text: "You're right about that. Prime Minister Alvarez's behavior during the meeting was appalling."

228.speaker: Player_Romus
228.text: "That's simply not true. Lespia has played and will continue to play an integral role in Trade Zone operations."

229.speaker: Player_Romus
229.text: "I'm not a fan of Lespia's profit-mongering either, but stripping them of their assets could be dangerous for everyone."

230.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
230.text: "Uh huh. The way Rumburg was uninvolved in the Wehlen Civil War?"

232.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
232.text: "We are trying to build a new ITZ. One that is not corrupted by western greed or selfish protectionist policies."

233.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
233.text: "There is no 'uninvolved', Mr. Toras. Either you are with us, or you are against us."

234.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
234.text: "As much as I personally dislike the man, he is a mere symptom of the disease called capitalism."

235.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
235.text: "You know what's dangerous? Allowing Lespia's selfish protectionist policies to slowly corrupt the new Trade Zone we are trying to build."

239.speaker: Narrator
239.text: He acknowledged my remark with a smile, then briskly moved over to the armoire.

240.speaker: Player_Romus
240.text: "I voted for nationalization. That alone should prove where my values lie."

241.speaker: Player_Romus
241.text: "I don't believe that. Rizia doesn't need to take any sides."

242.speaker: Player_Romus
242.text: "I want to side with you. But the repercussions with our allies would be too great."

243.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
243.text: "I am not asking you to openly side with us."

244.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
244.text: "I know that Prime Minister Saltana is meeting individually with you and Prime Minister Alvarez to come up with a nationalization plan for the MITZ."

245.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
245.text: "Yes, that alone was more than I expected."

246.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
246.text: "Allow me to explain what I want. Then we can discuss your supposed impartiality."

247.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
247.text: "You, King Romus, will not let that happen."

248.speaker: Player_Romus
248.text: "I don't know if I can. Lespia has a lot to offer Morella."

249.speaker: Player_Romus
249.text: "You have Prime Minister Saltana's ear. Why don't you just try to convince her to give Lespia the boot?"

250.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
250.text: "Lespia will do everything in its power to keep its operations running exactly as before."

251.speaker: Player_Romus
251.text: "That's easy. I was planning on making sure Lespia got the short end of the scepter anyway."

252.speaker: Player_Romus
252.text: "And how do you suggest we do that?"

253.speaker: Player_Romus
253.text: "But with Morella exercising central control over the MITZ, there'll be a limit to how much harm Lespia can do."

254.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
254.text: "That would be the ideal scenario. But Alvarez is very capable of weaseling out of it."

255.speaker: Player_Romus
255.text: "And how do you suggest we stop it?"

256.speaker: Player_Romus
256.text: "As Alvarez said, the MITZ would be nothing without Lespian mining technology. We can't ignore his country's contribution."

257.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
257.text: "Mining technology is worthless if the people operating it are being exploited."

258.speaker: Player_Romus
258.text: "We have a gas deal with Lespia. It wouldn't be wise to antagonize them."

263.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
263.text: "At the end of the day, I am only asking Rizia to act in its best interests."

264.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
264.text: "Valgsland's relationship with Morella is still young and fragile. I do not want us to be accused of overreach."

265.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
265.text: "You are Morella's direct neighbor and longtime ally. Ms. Saltana will surely be receptive to your offers."

266.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
266.text: "Do not let the deal fool you. Alvarez will stab you in the back at the slightest opportunity, especially after your board vote."

267.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
267.text: "Rizia, on the other hand, is Morella's direct neighbor and longtime ally. It's only natural that you would request a more favorable deal."

268.speaker: Player_Romus
268.text: "Outbidding Lespia may be in our best interests, but it will take a lot of resources. What can Valgsland offer us if I make this happen?"

269.speaker: Player_Romus
269.text: "It's not only about Rizia's interests. We need Lespia out for the good of the entire ITZ."

273.speaker: Player_Romus
273.text: "It would certainly be advantageous for Rizia to keep its foothold in the MITZ. If we end up with more than Lespia, so much the better."

274.speaker: Player_Romus
274.text: "You are suggesting that we act with the same greed you are accusing Lespia of."

275.speaker: Player_Romus
275.text: "It's not in our best interests to anger our powerful neighbor."

276.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
276.text: "I'm glad you agree. But I am happy to throw in another incentive."

278.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
278.text: "I know it will take much work. So I am happy to offer an incentive."

279.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
279.text: "I can tell you are not convinced. Allow me to offer an incentive."

280.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
280.text: "You voted in favor of nationalization. I trust any deal you make will still preserve the welfare of the MITZ's workers and the sovereignty of Morella."

281.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
281.text: "If you are still not convinced, I am happy to offer an incentive."

282.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
282.text: "Rizia's military weakness is no secret in international circles. Make sure Lespia ends up with nothing, and Valgsland will provide your navy with a significant upgrade."

283.speaker: Player_Romus
283.text: "You dare to call us weak, Mr. Hegel?"

284.speaker: Player_Romus
284.text: "Tempting. Our navy could use the help."

285.speaker: Player_Romus
285.text: "I'm afraid Valgslandian aid may be a red line for our partners in GRACE."

286.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
286.text: "Don't you think it's time to distance yourself from that network? You must know how isolated you are becoming."

287.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
287.text: "I don't need to convince you of Valgsland's dominion over the sea. Our warships and submarines are second to none."

288.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
288.text: "Perhaps that was a poor choice of phrasing. But you must admit that you cannot match Valgsland's dominion over the sea."

292.speaker: Player_Romus
292.text: "You're offering us a naval upgrade while we have forces stationed around a disputed gas field?"

293.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
293.text: "Why, yes. Perhaps Valgsland's superior vessels and equipment can help you solve that dispute faster."

294.speaker: Player_Romus
294.text: "I have had it with your disrespect. Remember that you are speaking to a king."

296.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
296.text: "Ha! Such titles mean nothing to me, Mr. Toras."

297.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
297.text: "Why should I respect you, when you don't respect the will of your own people?"

304.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
304.text: "Why should I respect a man who sits on a golden throne, surrounded by riches he did not earn?"

305.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
305.text: "Why should I respect a man who takes orders from some invisible being in the sky?"

306.speaker: Player_Romus
306.text: "Are you demeaning the Holy Spirit of St. Dast?"

307.speaker: Player_Romus
307.text: "Religion guides my decisions, yes, but I do not 'take orders' from anyone."

308.speaker: Player_Romus
308.text: "Like it or not, we are both world leaders. A little more decorum is in order."

309.speaker: Player_Romus
309.text: "Because I'm holding the cards. You're the one calling me in the middle of the night, remember?"

310.speaker: Player_Romus
310.text: "Take that back this instant. My people love me."

311.speaker: Narrator
311.text: There was a brief silence on the other end as Hegel seemed to collect himself.

312.speaker: Player_Romus
312.text: "My family earned everything we have. With the help of the Valgos Empire, I might add."

313.speaker: Player_Romus
313.text: "You are right. And in fact, I am trying to change the role of the monarchy in Rizia. Maybe you can help me."

315.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
315.text: "But please tell me. Can I count on your cooperation in the MITZ, or not?"

316.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
316.text: "Your people live in fear of you."

317.speaker: Narrator
317.text: There was a brief pause on the other end of the line.

318.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
318.text: "Whatever you want to call it, it should be completely separate from state matters."

319.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
319.text: "Sorry to wake you, Mr. Toras. This call was a mistake."

320.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
320.text: 'Even the smallest role played by religion in state matters is too large."

321.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
321.text: "The Valgos Empire is dead and gone. As the Kingdom of Rizia should be, by all rights."

324.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
324.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Turn02_Intention_ConstitutionalMonarchy"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Manus_ConstitutionalMonarchy"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Manus_OverthrowMonarchy"] == true) == false

325.speaker: Narrator
325.text: There was a brief pause on the other end of the line.

326.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
326.text: "Maybe I can. But for now, I want to know whether or not I can count on your cooperation in the MITZ."

327.speaker: Player_Romus
327.text: "Eventually, perhaps. But not with such a dramatic action."

328.speaker: Player_Romus
328.text: "Regardless, I am worried that accepting your republic's military assistance will send the wrong signal internationally."

329.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
329.text: "Voting for ITZ nationalization already aligned you with Valgsland. You may as well take advantage of it."

330.speaker: Player_Romus
330.text: "If I'm going to anger Lespia even further than I have already, it wouldn't hurt to have a stronger navy."

331.speaker: Player_Romus
331.text: "It'll send a strong signal. Too strong."

334.speaker: Player_Romus
334.text: "Yes. In exchange for your promised military aid, I will make sure Lespia walks away with nothing."

335.speaker: Player_Romus
335.text: "You can. But I'm not accepting your offer of naval reinforcements. Removing Lespian influence from the MITZ is enough of an incentive for me."

336.speaker: Player_Romus
336.text: "I'm sorry, but I can't promise you anything."

337.speaker: Player_Romus
337.text: "No. Given the magnitude of Lespia's investments in the MITZ, I can't go along with your plan."

341.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
341.text: "For a moment, I thought we had an understanding."

343.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
343.text: "And my offer will remain open should you change your mind."

344.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
344.text: "I will be sure to keep abreast of the negotiations."

346.speaker: Narrator
346.text: There was a silence, so long I began to think he had hung up.
346.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == false  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Trait_CommieKing"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Pales_ANDORArbitration"] == true) == false)

347.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
347.text: "You might want to know that I have been contacted by your daughter."

351.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
351.text: "I may be overstepping my boundaries. But I cannot shake the feeling that you and I want the same thing for Rizia."

353.speaker: Player_Romus
353.text: "Wait. I do want to help squeeze Lespia out of the Trade Zone. You can count on my cooperation."

354.speaker: Player_Romus
354.text: "Until you treat the Rizian monarchy with more deference, we will remain at odds."

356.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
356.text: "Good, Mr. Toras. But do not expect any military aid from Valgsland."

357.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
357.text: "Then we will be at odds for eternity."

358.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
358.text: "Good night. And give my regards to the Princess."

369.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
369.text: "You have already deployed your military to the Antacean. No use in half measures."

370.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
370.text: "You are a rational man. You must admit that the monarchical system belongs in the dustbin of history."

371.speaker: Player_Romus
371.text: "It's almost as if you want to help Rizia retake Pales."

376.speaker: Player_Romus
376.text: "My councilors were already against ITZ nationalization. They will certainly be against further cooperation with Valgsland."

377.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
377.text: "You're the king, aren't you? You make the decisions."

378.speaker: Player_Romus
378.text: "That's not surprising. She goes where her intellectual curiosity takes her."

379.speaker: Player_Romus
379.text: "I'm sorry, Chancellor. The princess can be a real brat sometimes."

380.speaker: Player_Romus
380.text: "So *that*'s what she's been doing during my council meetings."

381.speaker: Player_Romus
381.text: "What?! You are to cease your communication with her at once."

385.speaker: Narrator
385.text: There was a silence, so long I began to think he had hung up.
385.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == false  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Trait_CommieKing"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Trait_CommieKing"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Military_Valgsland_AcceptNavalAid"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Pales_ANDORArbitration"] == true) == false)

389.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
389.text: "On the contrary. She's got a brilliant mind."

390.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
390.text: "If you're not involving the Princess in politics, you should be. She has a brilliant mind."

391.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
391.text: "Why? From her letters and our conversation, I have the sense that the two of you want the same thing for Rizia."

392.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
392.text: "And from my communications, I have the sense that both of you want the same thing for Rizia."

394.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
394.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == false  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Trait_CommieKing"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Trait_CommieKing"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Military_Valgsland_AcceptNavalAid"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Pales_ANDORArbitration"] == true) == false)

395.speaker: Player_Romus
395.text: "You don't need to call me that."

399.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
399.text: "Don't get me wrong -- I despise monarchies. But I do occasionally wonder whether my job would be easier if I could sidestep the government infighting."

404.speaker: Player_Romus
404.text: "Disagreement is part of any healthy government. Monarchical or not."

405.speaker: Player_Romus
405.text: "A paradox, isn't it? The more opinions you entertain in the name of representation, the harder it is to give your people what they actually need."

406.speaker: Player_Romus
406.text: "I can't act with total impunity. My hands are tied by royal tradition."

407.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
407.text: "That tradition was established by men in your exact same position. You have the power to break it."

408.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
408.text: "Yet the longer one holds absolute power, the further one becomes distanced from those needs."

409.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
409.text: "Ha. No, in the end I would never allow myself to override my government's checks and balances."

410.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
410.text: "You're correct, of course. Just an idle musing."

411.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
411.text: "You can expect the delivery of new vessels and equipment as soon as the nationalization agreement is finalized."

412.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
412.text: "Can I count on your cooperation or not?"

413.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
413.text: "But enough about our governments. I want to know whether I can count on your cooperation."

414.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
414.text: "Just tell me. Can I count on your cooperation?"

415.speaker: Player_Romus
415.text: "You are going too far, Mr. Hegel. You shall speak to me with the respect a king deserves."

416.speaker: Player_Romus
416.text: "I disagree. In fact, a truly benevolent king can meet his people's needs more efficiently than a squabbling parliament."

417.speaker: Player_Romus
417.text: "Even if I agreed with you, cutting ties with Rumburg would be a disaster for us."

418.speaker: Player_Romus
418.text: "Actually, combining a democratic system with the benefits of having a reigning sovereign seems like the best of both worlds to me."

419.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
419.text: "Or an opportunity for new connections. Ones that will bind you with Merkopa's future, not its past."

424.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
424.text: "No man or woman should be placed above all others, even symbolically."

425.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
425.text: "I wouldn't say that. But there's one point on which we may agree."

426.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
426.text: "Regretfully, yes But there's still one point on which we may agree."

427.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
427.text: "I am happy you see it that way."

428.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
428.text: "And I with monarchies. But there is one point on which we may agree."

429.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
429.text: "Normally, no. But there is one point on which we may agree."

430.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
430.text: "Different as we are, there is one point on which we may agree."

431.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
431.text: "The Republic of Lespia does not belong in the Meftiem International Trade Zone."

432.speaker: Player_Romus
432.text: "Another east-west battle? You should know that as a member of GRACE, Rizia is obliged to stay uninvolved."

433.speaker: Player_Romus
433.text: "I agree that Prime Minister Alvarez's behavior during the meeting was appalling."

434.speaker: Player_Romus
434.text: "You are wrong about that. Lespia has played and will continue to play an integral role in Trade Zone operations."

435.speaker: Player_Romus
435.text: "You heard what I said in the meeting. Neither Lespia nor Rizia will accept any change in the way the MITZ is run."

436.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
436.text: "Uh huh. The way Rumburg was uninvolved in the Wehlen Civil War?"

438.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
438.text: "There is no 'uninvolved', Mr. Toras. Either you are on the side of the working man, or you are against him."

439.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
439.text: "As much as I personally dislike the man, he is a mere symptom of the disease called capitalism."

440.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
440.text: "Yet Morella and Valgsland will not accept the status quo. So what are we to do?"

445.speaker: Player_Romus
445.text: "I don't believe that. One can sympathize with the plight of the working man without going full-on revolutionary."

446.speaker: Player_Romus
446.text: "Then I suppose I am against him. Sorry."

448.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
448.text: "I don't think you understand what's happening right now."

450.speaker: Player_Romus
450.text: "Rizia and Lespia will stand together in preserving the status quo."

454.speaker: Player_Romus
454.text: "We want better conditions for Morellan workers. But not at the expense of Rizian or Lespian interests."

456.speaker: Player_Romus
456.text: "That's where we disagree. I don't like Alvarez as a person, but we are fighting for the same principles."

457.speaker: Player_Romus
457.text: "Like Lespia, we are committed to working together with Morella to build a more equitable ITZ."

458.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
458.text: "Let me lay it out for you, Mr. Toras."

459.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
459.text: "Prime Minister Saltana is planning to reopen negotiations on the MITZ profit-sharing agreement. Any new version will have to be approved by three out of the four countries on the board."

460.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
460.text: "Say you wanted to make an agreement where Lespia came away with nothing. As long as Valgsland approved it, it would still pass."

462.speaker: Player_Romus
462.text: "What exactly do you want, Mr. Hegel?"

463.speaker: Player_Romus
463.text: "Obviously, either Valgsland or Morella must make a compromise."

465.speaker: Player_Romus
465.text: "Stay in a stalemate until one country caves. But it won't be Rizia."

466.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
466.text: "And we are willing to do so. Under one condition."

467.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
467.text: "Please, Mr. Toras. Rizia is not in any position to start a war with anyone."

471.speaker: Player_Romus
471.text: "You want me to screw over my business partner."

472.speaker: Player_Romus
472.text: "You want me to screw Mr. Alvarez over."

474.speaker: Player_Romus
474.text: "You have Prime Minister Saltana's ear. Why aren't you saying this to her?"

475.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
475.text: "Valgsland's relationship with Morella is still young and fragile. I do not want us to be accused of overreach."

476.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
476.text: "Rizia, on the other hand, is Morella's direct neighbor and longtime ally. It's only natural that you would request a more favorable deal than Lespia."

477.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
477.text: "Make no mistake. Alvarez will do exactly the same thing if given the slightest opportunity."

478.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
478.text: "I wouldn't call it a 'partnership'. Alvarez will do exactly the same thing if given the slightest opportunity."

479.speaker: Player_Romus
479.text: "I think I know what you're getting at. And I like it."

480.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
480.text: "Both of you will soon be invited to Morella for negotiations. I want you to make sure Lespia receives as small of a share as possible."

481.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
481.text: "At the end of the day, I am only asking you to act in Rizia's best interests."

482.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
482.text: "You'll be invited to Morella for negotiations soon. I want you to make sure Lespia receives as small of a share as possible."

483.speaker: Player_Romus
483.text: "I am all for trying to out-negotiate Lespia, but I'm afraid Rizia doesn't have the resources. Can you offer us any help?"

484.speaker: Player_Romus
484.text: "It's not only about Rizia. We need to limit Arcasian influence in the Trade Zone."

488.speaker: Player_Romus
488.text: "It would certainly be advantageous for Rizia to keep our share of ITZ profits. If we end up with more than Lespia, so much the better."

489.speaker: Player_Romus
489.text: "It's in our interests to work out a deal with Lespia and Morella. Valgsland's input is irrelevant."

490.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
490.text: "Approving the final agreement will be help enough, I should think."

491.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
491.text: "I'm glad you see it that way."

494.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
494.text: "Needless to say, we still expect that you will make up for the way Rizia treated Morella over the years."

495.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
495.text: "Needless to say, we still expect that you will make up for the way Rizia treated Morella over the years."

496.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
496.text: "Needless to say, we still expect that you will make up for the way Rizia treated Morella over the years."

497.speaker: Player_Romus
497.text: "If it means that much to you, I will make it happen."

499.speaker: Player_Romus
499.text: "I would anyway. Just because I voted against nationalization doesn't mean I'm heartless."

500.speaker: Narrator
500.text: I could hear irritation in his voice.

501.speaker: Player_Romus
501.text: "You're in no position to make demands, Chancellor. You're the one calling me in the middle of the night."

506.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
506.text: "You denied better working conditions to your own countrymen. You'll excuse my skepticism."

508.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
508.text: "It should mean something to you. If you are the benevolent leader you claim to be."

510.speaker: Player_Romus
510.text: "It's in my best interests to side with Lespia. As I have already agreed to do."

514.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
514.text: "And you don't think that Lespia is angling for Morella's favor even as we speak?"

517.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
517.text: "Valgsland cannot publicly support a monarchy like Rizia. Especially after the way you voted."

518.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
518.text: "But we can sell you our naval equipment, which, as I need not remind you, is vastly superior to Rizia's own."

519.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
519.text: "Make sure Lespia winds up with nothing, and Valgsland will assist you with a significant upgrade."

520.speaker: Player_Romus
520.text: "Are you implying that our military is weak, Mr. Hegel?"

521.speaker: Player_Romus
521.text: "I'm afraid Valgslandian aid would be a red line for our partners in GRACE."

522.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
522.text: "It would not be aid. We would only make our vessels and equipment available for purchase."

523.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
523.text: "I don't need to convince you of Valgsland's dominion over the sea. Our warships and submarines are second to none."

524.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
524.text: "Excuse my phrasing. But you must admit that you cannot match Valgsland's dominion over the sea."

525.speaker: Player_Romus
525.text: "You're offering us a naval upgrade while we already have forces stationed around a disputed gas field?"

526.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
526.text: "Why, yes. Perhaps Valgsland's superior vessels and equipment can help you solve that dispute faster."

527.speaker: Player_Romus
527.text: "Tempting. Our navy could use the help."

531.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
531.text: "Besides which, you should not care about the opinion of a group of inbred despots."

532.speaker: Player_Romus
532.text: "Still, my councilors will be against any form of cooperation with Valgsland."

533.speaker: Player_Romus
533.text: "It'll send a strong signal. Too strong."

537.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
537.text: "You have already deployed your military to the Antacean. No use in half measures."

538.speaker: Player_Romus
538.text: "It's almost as if you want to help Rizia retake Pales."

540.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
540.text: "Isn't that the sole benefit of being a monarch? You can make decisions without spending months bogged down in government infighting."

542.speaker: Player_Romus
542.text: "Disagreement is part of any healthy government. Monarchical or not."

543.speaker: Player_Romus
543.text: "Is that a problem in Valgsland? Trying to please everyone, ending up pleasing no one?"

544.speaker: Player_Romus
544.text: "I can't act with total impunity. My hands are tied by royal tradition."

545.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
545.text: "That tradition was established by men in your exact same position. You have the power to break it."

546.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
546.text: "It is still better than allowing unlimited power to blind you to your people's true needs."

547.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
547.text: "Ha. No, in the end I would never allow myself to override my government's checks and balances."

548.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
548.text: "You're correct, of course. Just an idle musing."

549.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
549.text: "But enough about our governments. I want to know whether I can count on your cooperation."

550.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
550.text: "Just tell me. Can I count on your cooperation?"

554.speaker: Player_Romus
554.text: "If I'm going to stab Lespia in the back, Rizia will definitely need to be able to defend itself afterwards."

555.speaker: Player_Romus
555.text: "I am putting my foot down. We neither need nor want your assistance."

556.speaker: Player_Romus
556.text: "You hope to win me over by demeaning me and the institution I stand for? Show some respect."

558.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
558.text: "Very well. It was only an offer."

559.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
559.text: "So can I count on your cooperation?"

560.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
560.text: "Why should I respect you, when you don't respect the will of your own people?"

567.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
567.text: "Why should I respect a man who sits on a golden throne, surrounded by riches he did not earn?"

568.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
568.text: "Why should I respect a man who takes orders from some invisible being in the sky?"

569.speaker: Player_Romus
569.text: "Are you demeaning the Holy Spirit of St. Dast?"

570.speaker: Player_Romus
570.text: "Religion guides my decisions, yes, but I do not 'take orders' from anyone."

571.speaker: Player_Romus
571.text: "Like it or not, we are both world leaders. A little more decorum is in order."

572.speaker: Player_Romus
572.text: "Because I'm holding the cards. You're the one calling me in the middle of the night, remember?"

573.speaker: Player_Romus
573.text: "Take that back this instant. My people love me."

574.speaker: Narrator
574.text: There was a brief pause on the other end of the line.

575.speaker: Narrator
575.text: There was silence on the other end as Hegel seemed to collect himself.

576.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
576.text: "The Valgos Empire is dead and gone. As the Kingdom of Rizia should be, by all rights."

578.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
578.text: "Your people live in fear of you."

579.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
579.text: "Whatever you want to call it, it should be completely separate from state matters."

580.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
580.text: 'Even the smallest role played by religion in state matters is too large."

583.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
583.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Turn02_Intention_ConstitutionalMonarchy"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Manus_ConstitutionalMonarchy"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Manus_OverthrowMonarchy"] == true) == false

584.speaker: Player_Romus
584.text: "My family earned everything we have. With the help of the Valgos Empire, I might add."

585.speaker: Player_Romus
585.text: "You are right. And in fact, I am trying to change the role of the monarchy in Rizia. Maybe you can help me."

587.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
587.text: "But if you do need a further incentive..."

588.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
588.text: "Sorry to wake you, Mr. Toras. This call was a mistake."

590.speaker: Player_Romus
590.text: "Wait. I do want to help squeeze Lespia out of the Trade Zone. You can count on my cooperation."

591.speaker: Player_Romus
591.text: "Until you treat the Rizian monarchy with more deference, we will remain at odds."

594.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
594.text: "Then we will be at odds for eternity."

595.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
595.text: "Good night. And give my regards to the Princess."

607.speaker: Player_Romus
607.text: "One of those 'despots' is my sister-in-law. And losing her favor would be disastrous for us."

608.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
608.text: "Or an opportunity for new connections. Ones that will bind you with Merkopa's future, not its past."

609.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
609.text: "Monarchist or not, you have shown me where your priorities lie."

610.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
610.text: "For now, just tell me. Can I count on your cooperation?"

611.speaker: Player_Romus
611.text: "You can. In exchange for the navy deal you mentioned, I will shrink Lespia's share of the MITZ."

612.speaker: Player_Romus
612.text: "I cannot promise anything. But it's good to know that Valgsland will support Rizia getting a larger profit share."

613.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
613.text: "In that case, I cannot promise anything in that arena either. I will have to see the final proposal."

614.speaker: Player_Romus
614.text: "There will be no cooperation between Rizia and Valgsland, Mr. Hegel. On MITZ matters or otherwise."

617.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
617.text: "For some reason, my people are crazy about the Rizian royal family. Because of your history with the Valgos Empire, I suppose."

618.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
618.text: "But you're no better than Lespia. Prime Minister Saltana will see right through you both."

619.speaker: Player_Romus
619.text: "Not on this matter. But I do not wish to be on bad terms with Valgsland."

621.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
621.text: "Thank you. I am glad this phone call was not a waste of both of our time."

623.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
623.text: "For some reason, my people are crazy about the Rizian royal family. Because of your history with the Valgos Empire, perhaps."

625.speaker: Player_Romus
625.text: "Everyone loves royals, Chancellor. Even die-hard socialists."

626.speaker: Player_Romus
626.text: "Are you saying it's time to revive those old ties?"

627.speaker: Player_Romus
627.text: "Funny. My people don't feel the same about Valgish aristocrats."

628.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
628.text: "Because there aren't any more of them. Except the ones in Pales."

629.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
629.text: "I'm not saying anything. Just thinking out loud."

630.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
630.text: "Your lifestyle inspires jealousy. If not your familial squabbles and the constant scrutiny you're under."

633.speaker: Player_Romus
633.text: "You are sorely mistaken. Neither of us want that."

634.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
634.text: "You should speak with your daughter more often, Mr. Toras."

636.speaker: Player_Romus
636.text: "You will not speak of this again, Mr. Hegel. And you will cut off contact with Vina immediately."

637.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
637.text: "Ah. Perhaps I was mistaken about your intentions."

639.speaker: Player_Romus
639.text: "We cannot have this conversation now. We must wait until the time is right."

641.speaker: Player_Romus
641.text: "*If* that was what I wanted, how could Valgsland help me?"

642.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
642.text: "Later, Mr. Toras. I await the results of your visit to Morella."

644.speaker: Player_Romus
644.text: "How dare you even suggest that? Don't make me regret working with you."

645.speaker: Player_Romus
645.text: "Capitalism is what kept the MITZ running all these years. I would not disparage it."

649.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
649.text: "I will, however, support Rizia in your current arbitration case against Pales."

650.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
650.text: "Not out of any loyalty to you, but because I believe the sovereign territory of islands must be respected."

651.speaker: Player_Romus
651.text: "You have our gratitude for that, good sir."

653.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
653.text: "You're getting it anyway. If the AN decides to disrespect the sovereign territory of islands, Rizia is not the only country that will suffer for it."

655.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
655.text: "You must have some inkling why. If the AN decides to disrespect the sovereign territory of islands, Rizia is not the only country that will suffer for it."

659.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
659.text: "And incidentally, you can count on Valgsland's support in your current arbitration case against Pales."

660.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
660.text: "I believe Rizia deserves it. But more importantly, the AN must respect the sovereign territory of islands."

661.speaker: Player_Romus
661.text: "You have our gratitude for that, good sir."

662.speaker: Player_Romus
662.text: "You're just full of favors today, aren't you?"

694.speaker: Player_Romus
694.text: "Titus told me what you were up to the night Father died."
694.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Turn05_MurderInvest_SuspectPabel"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.PoisonInvestigator_Lucita"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Pabel_OutedToPlayer"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Turn05_MurderInvest_SuspectPabel"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.PoisonInvestigator_Titus"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Pabel_OutedToPlayer"] == true)

695.speaker: Narrator
695.text: Pabel hurriedly draped my robe over my shoulders. He turned to face me.

696.speaker: Pabel Adria
696.text: "You investigated me? I told you I was innocent."

698.speaker: Player_Romus
698.text: "Right. I bet I can guess what you were tasting."

702.speaker: Player_Romus
702.text: "I thought you were in love with me all this time."

704.speaker: Pabel Adria
704.text: "That doesn't mean I was a eunuch."

705.speaker: Pabel Adria
705.text: "I don't know what you're talking about, Your Majesty. I was conducting a tasting session with a Cantuavo representative."

706.speaker: Player_Romus
706.text: "It's all fine. They didn't turn up any conclusive evidence against you."

707.speaker: Narrator
707.text: Pabel let out a quiet sigh of relief.

708.speaker: Player_Romus
708.text: "I don't care what you call it. Keep carrying on like this and I'll have you thrown in prison."

709.speaker: Narrator
709.text: He opened his mouth in denial, then shut it.

711.speaker: Player_Romus
711.text: "It's all right. Your secret is still safe with me."

712.speaker: Narrator
712.text: Pabel breathed a sigh of relief.

713.speaker: Player_Romus
713.text: "I don't care what you do after hours. But you've got to be more careful."

717.speaker: Player_Romus
717.text: "Sorry, Pabel. I couldn't leave any stone unturned."

718.speaker: Pabel Adria
718.text: "Well, it's been turned now. Am I under arrest?"

720.speaker: Pabel Adria
720.text: "Well, now you know. I was conducting a tasting session with a Cantuavo representative."

724.speaker: Player_Romus
724.text: "It's nothing personal. I couldn't make it look like I was playing favorites."

726.speaker: Pabel Adria
726.text: "You're lucky they didn't turn up anything on the two of us."

728.speaker: Player_Romus
728.text: "No. And the very possibility is ridiculous."

729.speaker: Player_Romus
729.text: "You would be if there was more evidence. Consider yourself lucky."

730.speaker: Player_Romus
730.text: "No, but the Lord knows what you did."

732.speaker: Pabel Adria
732.text: "Believe me, I do. Nothing like this will happen again."

736.speaker: Pabel Adria
736.text: "I... I have repented since then. I swear."

737.speaker: Pabel Adria
737.text: "Carrying on like what? If you want me to stop controlling the quality of the palace wine, I will."

738.speaker: Pabel Adria
738.text: "Anyway... it's quite an urgent phone call."

741.speaker: Player_Romus
741.text: "It's ludicrous. If it were a woman, you'd get a slap on the wrist at worst. But a man..."

742.speaker: Player_Romus
742.text: "How many of you are out there?"

747.speaker: Player_Romus
747.text: "You cannot order me around, Chancellor. Be more mindful of your words of choice."

749.speaker: Player_Romus
749.text: "Lucita is on your trail, though. Don't do anything stupid. Or anyone."

753.speaker: Player_Romus
753.text: "Titus is on your trail, though. Don't do anything stupid. Or anyone."

754.speaker: Pabel Adria
754.text: "I won't. Thank you for telling me."

759.speaker: Player_Romus
759.text: "It's all right. Your secret is safe with me."
